clue.text: Daughter in request to have nightie

indicators.note: in says the daughter's letter is placed inside the word for a request

parts.note: to request is to beg
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: A daughter pleads to be allowed a nightdress of her own.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedgown is an old word for a nightgown worn in bed, so a nightie is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Stirring material, Mozart's finale in symphony

indicators.note: in places the closing letter inside the name of the symphony

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony

indicators.note: a finale is the end, so take the last letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A music critic finds the closing movement of a Mozart symphony moving.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Mozart's is possessive: the finale belongs to the name, giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic writing or art is material intended to arouse, which is what stirring hints at.

clue.text: Novelist from Greece New Yorker's behind

parts.note: GR is the international abbreviation for Greece
an American would call the backside the ass

explanation.surface: A writer from Greece turns out to be one of the New Yorker magazine's contributors.
explanation.definitionFit: Günter Grass was the German novelist who wrote The Tin Drum.

clue.text: Rest freely in city like 3, 10, 17, 22 and 28?

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the city

parts.note: the Wen is an old name for London, Cobbett's 'Great Wen'

indicators.note: freely says the letters of rest are let loose to form a new order

explanation.surface: Someone takes a relaxed break in a city, with a puzzling list of cross-references attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wen is Cobbett's nickname for London. The cross-references are grass, cola, jeans, Brandt (chancellor of West Germany) and liberty, all emblems of the Cold War West.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of those referenced answers is associated with the West: Cold War symbols of the capitalist bloc.

clue.text: Follow clothing model's size problem

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the word for follow encloses the other piece

parts.note: to follow orders is to obey
to model for an artist is to sit

explanation.surface: A fashion model's dress follows the trend, yet sizing remains an issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Being severely overweight is a health problem defined by body size.

clue.text: Biographer lacking content on real playwright

indicators.note: lacking content means the inside of the word is emptied, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: echt is a German borrowing meaning genuine or real

explanation.surface: A biographer with nothing to say writes about a real-life dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertolt Brecht was the German dramatist behind Mother Courage.

clue.text: Very large revolutionary claim is constructed — by this theory?

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the letters for very large run backwards

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: constructed says the letters of claim is are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A huge revolutionary claim is put together; is this the theory behind it?
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' and 'constructed' do double duty in the surface, suggesting the political revolution the theory inspired.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark hints that a revolutionary claim to public ownership is exactly the political doctrine meant.

clue.text: Ancient hero outside of Seattle in America

indicators.note: in puts the picked letters inside the name for America

parts.note: America is often called the US, with the article

indicators.note: outside of tells us to take only the outer letters of the city's name

explanation.surface: An old-time hero is spotted on the edge of Seattle in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian who slew the Minotaur is a mythical Greek hero.

clue.text: Hilbert working with all new element of long division

indicators.note: working means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: The mathematician Hilbert works on fresh material for a long-division exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests arithmetic; the division is the long split between East and West Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: The barrier was a physical element in Germany's decades-long partition.

clue.text: Pass one soft drink

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone declines one fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cola is a sweet carbonated beverage, a kind of soft drink.

clue.text: Plot ousting Allende ultimately transformed Chile? He defended Reds' goal

indicators.note: ousting means removing one letter from the word for plot

parts.note: a plot is a scheme

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the name
transformed says the letters of the country are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A coup that deposed Salvador Allende changed Chile for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting' removes E (Allende's last letter) from SCHEME to give SCHME; 'transformed' turns CHILE into ICHEL. The Reds are Manchester United, a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Schmeichel was the Danish goalkeeper for Manchester United, nicknamed the Red Devils.

clue.text: Front of tabloid magazine's web

indicators.note: front of points to the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a single edition of a magazine is an issue

explanation.surface: The cover of a tabloid magazine is shown on its website.
explanation.definitionFit: A web of connective cells is tissue; also a fine woven fabric.

clue.text: European leader having retired, like Louis XVI

indicators.note: having means holding, so the word for retired contains the other pieces

parts.note: one who has retired for the night has gone to bed
a leader is the head

explanation.surface: A European ruler has stepped down, like the last king of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The French king lost his head on the guillotine in 1793, so he was decapitated.

clue.text: Somewhat bombastic ass and rather a doom-monger

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pompous fool is more or less a prophet of gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Trojan prophetess foretold disaster and was never believed, so her name means a pessimist.

clue.text: Stars smoke cannabis around queen in feverish condition

parts.note: suns are stars

indicators.note: around says the cannabis word wraps the royal letter

parts.note: to toke is to smoke a joint
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: Celebrities smoke pot around a queen and end up feverish.
explanation.definitionFit: Heatstroke from overexposure to the sun brings fever and collapse.

clue.text: Clean river around Kent area?

parts.note: around a place can mean in it
Kent is a county in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A tidy river somewhere in the Kent region.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash something through with water is to clean it.

clue.text: Girl's or French man's clothes

definitions.meaning: belonging to a girl named Jean
belonging to a Frenchman named Jean

explanation.surface: Clothes that belong either to a girl or to a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean is both an English girl's name and a French man's name; in plural they are denim trousers.

clue.text: People honourably discharged from service merit indulgence

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Veterans released from duty deserve some pampering.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired professors keep their title as an honour, so they are retirees honourably released.

clue.text: Rock to hit sheltering bug or insect

indicators.note: sheltering means enclosing, so the shuffled letters wrap the bug
Rock means shake up, so the letters of to hit are rearranged

parts.note: a germ is a bug, as in a stomach bug

explanation.surface: A boulder hits a bug or other creepy-crawly that has taken cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal; 'bug' looks like the insect but is a germ.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger moth is a striped moth, which is an insect.

clue.text: Spring festival given name like 6, 7, 21s and the 25?

parts.note: Easter is the spring festival

explanation.surface: A spring holiday gets named after a list of cross-references.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references are Brecht, socialism, Trabants and the Stasi.
explanation.definitionFit: All of those referenced answers belong to the Eastern bloc, especially East Germany.

clue.text: Bishop drawing up, with worker's car

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
drawing is art
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A bishop sketching alongside a labourer's motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses B + ART to give TRAB.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trabant was the small East German car built from plastic resin.

clue.text: Willy starts to become relaxed after nine double tequilas

indicators.note: starts to means take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Willy begins to loosen up after nine double tequilas.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Brandt was the West German chancellor known for his Ostpolitik.

clue.text: Ambassador has a fling in get-away location

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
a fling is a throw

explanation.surface: A diplomat has an affair at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' seems romantic but means a toss.
explanation.definitionFit: London's main airport is a place where people depart on holiday.

clue.text: Prance around, always following band

indicators.note: following says the word for always comes after the band

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth
ay is an old poetic word for ever

explanation.surface: Someone dances about for ever behind a band.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounce or strut showily is to walk with a swaggering prance.

clue.text: Mostly inactive state police

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter

parts.note: stasis is a state of inactivity

explanation.surface: State police are largely idle.
explanation.definitionFit: The secret police force of East Germany was known by this name.

clue.text: Orchestral passage left in dancing reel intro

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the rearranged letters
dancing means the letters of reel intro move around

explanation.surface: A section of music is dropped into the introduction of a lively reel.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritornello is an instrumental refrain between vocal sections, in older spelling.

clue.text: Fabled warrior's club

definitions.meaning: the Greek hero of the Trojan War

explanation.surface: A legendary fighter's weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax is both a Homeric hero at Troy and a famous Dutch football club.

clue.text: Monarch totally disheartened after politician creates free state

indicators.note: after says the monarch and the next piece come after the politician

parts.note: a Lib is a Liberal politician
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart, leaving just the outer letters

explanation.surface: A ruler, dispirited after a politician sets up an independent state.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free is a state of freedom.

clue.text: Team heading for extra time in some distress

indicators.note: in places the team and other letters inside the word for some

parts.note: any means some
XI is a team of eleven, as in cricket or football

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A team heads into extra time feeling stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Worry and unease are mental distress.
